eol_detection_delay.delay_interpretation: Model detected permanent EOL 1 cycles EARLY (actual: cycle 125, predicted: cycle 124). Conservative — model is cautious near end of life.

drift_onset.note: No sustained systematic drift detected with current parameters. The model's signed error does not show a persistent positive shift above the threshold.

hypothesis_evaluation.hypothesis: Late-life predictions are less reliable than early/mid-life predictions
findings: Late-life MAE (0.11%) exceeds early-life MAE (0.10%) — prediction accuracy degrades in late life.
Late-life signed bias is +0.00% (systematic overestimation of SoH).
EOL detected 1 cycles early — model is conservative.
hypothesis_evaluation.conclusion: SUPPORTED — 2/3 criteria met. The AI model shows measurable degradation in prediction quality during late-life battery operation.

eol_detection_delay.delay_interpretation: Model detected permanent EOL at exactly the correct cycle (122). No detection delay.

hypothesis_evaluation.hypothesis: Late-life predictions are less reliable than early/mid-life predictions

eol_detection_delay.delay_interpretation: Actual permanent EOL at cycle 123, but model predictions never permanently crossed the 70% threshold — model fails to detect EOL.

drift_onset.note: Drift onset detected at cycle 100 (75.6% of lifecycle). Rolling bias exceeded threshold (3.299%) for 5+ consecutive windows.

hypothesis_evaluation.hypothesis: Late-life predictions are less reliable than early/mid-life predictions
findings: Late-life MAE (3.26%) exceeds early-life MAE (1.60%) — prediction accuracy degrades in late life.
Late-life signed bias is +3.26% (systematic overestimation of SoH).
EOL detection is delayed by 9 cycles — model fails to flag end-of-life in a timely manner.
hypothesis_evaluation.conclusion: SUPPORTED — 3/3 criteria met. The AI model shows measurable degradation in prediction quality during late-life battery operation.

aggregate_results.overall_conclusion: The late-life prediction degradation hypothesis is supported by 2/4 NASA batteries. Mean late-life MAE (0.8841%) vs early-life MAE (0.481%). Mean late-life signed bias: +0.82%.
